title: Governance framework for redesigning advisory committees
subtitle: Also: updated Mayor and Council expense and education policy, and recognition of staff awards.
overview: The committee's main item was a new governance framework for the City's advisory committees of Council, developed with the Guelph Lab and the University of Guelph. It sets common commitments for every committee and a four-stage process for creating, running and evaluating them. The committee recommended that Council approve the framework {{vote:m2}}.

Staff will now apply the framework to each existing committee, which could lead to changes in mandates, scope or mergers, and report back in the fourth quarter of 2024. Recruitment and appointments to these committees will pause until then, except where needed to keep a quorum. The Clerk will also study random sampling as a way to recruit more representative members, and budget costs go to future multi-year budgets. Residents who serve or hope to serve on these committees will see the biggest effect.

The committee also recommended approving an updated Mayor and Council expense and education policy, which replaces the policy on councillor attendance at municipal events {{vote:m1}}. Members also recognized staff and partners for awards and certifications, including the City Treasurer's provincial leadership award. Council will consider all of these recommendations later.

decisions.item: Mayor and Council expense and education policy
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the updated policy and repeal the Policy on Councillor Attendance at Municipal Events.
The committee recommended that Council approve the Advisory Committees of Council Governance Framework set out in report 2023-413.
The committee recommended directing staff, with the Guelph Lab and University of Guelph, to apply the framework to existing advisory committees and report back in Q4 2024.
The committee recommended that the City Clerk prepare annual information reports from 2025 on how the framework is being implemented.
The committee recommended that the City Clerk research random representative sampling for appointments and report back before the 2028-2031 multi-year budget.

decisions.item: Pause on recruitment and budget referral
decisions.detail: The committee recommended pausing advisory committee recruitment and appointments until Q4 2024, except to maintain quorum, and referring the framework's budget implications to future multi-year budgets.

debate: Several councillors asked whether the framework wording gave advisory committees too strong a role in setting strategic goals. One councillor suggested the commitment say committees should "help shape" those goals, since Council makes the final decision. Staff and the researchers were open to the change, and the Mayor suggested the wording be settled with staff before Council's vote later in the month.

Councillors raised resourcing. One said that the deliberative approach, with more research, meetings and staff preparation, could need more than the budget now includes. Staff said the framework would be supported for a limited number of committees, that its pace depends on resources, and that more resources would be needed to move faster.

On councillors sitting on advisory committees, the researchers reported that everyone they consulted supported not appointing them, though Council could still make exceptions, as it did for Heritage Guelph. Councillors spoke in favour of keeping committees independent of councillor influence while recommendations are being developed.

Councillors asked about evaluation and recruitment. Evaluation is set at a minimum cycle to avoid burdening committees, and extra reviews or exit interviews are possible. Staff said the recruitment pause avoids recruiting for mandates that may soon change and protects staff capacity for the review.

Other questions covered the cost of staff time spent supporting committees, which is not tracked now, and whether a proposed permanent Clerk's Office position would add to departmental support (staff said it would). A councillor also asked that Council reports link to the relevant committee meeting minutes or video.
